title: Balm issue #211: JEI integration causes massive memory leak / system crash on Fabric 1.21.11

text:
[issue by The0GReborn]
### Minecraft Version

1.21.11

### Mod Loader

Fabric

### Describe the Issue

Hi there,

I’ve been trying to use JEI in a Fabric modpack I put together, but JEI is consuming RAM extremely fast and eventually causes the entire system to freeze or crash.

Before adding JEI, I was able to run the modpack without any issues, with total memory usage staying around ~2 GB. After adding JEI, memory usage rapidly increases to 5–6 GB, even though Minecraft is only allocated 4 GB of RAM. On my system (8 GB total RAM), this results in heavy paging and an OS-level freeze.

The issue consistently occurs during JEI initialization and when opening the inventory (JEI UI). Removing JEI immediately fixes the problem.

Steps to Reproduce

Use SKLauncher

Create a Fabric profile for Minecraft 1.21.11

Allocate 4 GB RAM

Use the following JVM arguments:

-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions
-XX:+UseG1GC
-XX:G1NewSizePercent=20
-XX:G1ReservePercent=20
-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=50
-XX:G1HeapRegionSize=16M
-Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true


Install the following mods:

Fabric API (latest for 1.21.11)

Balm (Fabric, 1.21.11)

Tom’s Storage (Fabric, 1.21.11)

Launch Minecraft and confirm memory usage is stable (~2 GB)

Exit the game

Add Just Enough Items (JEI) (latest Fabric build)

Launch Minecraft again

Load a world and open the inventory

Result

Memory usage rapidly increases from ~2 GB to 5–6 GB

JVM heap remains limited to 4 GB, but total system memory keeps growing

Severe lag occurs, followed by a full system freeze or crash

Control Test

Removing JEI while keeping all other mods installed returns memory usage to normal and the game runs stably.

Machine Specs

CPU: Intel i3 (older generation)

RAM: 8 GB

GPU: Intel HD Graphics (shared memory)

OS: Windows

Java: Java 25 (also reproducible on Java 21, but slower)

[comment by The0GReborn (none)]
The mod are documented in the log. The crash occurred while loading terrain.

[comment by BlayTheNinth (member)]
JEI integrations in 1.21.11 were temporarily removed due to incompatible renames of Vanilla code. 

Neither Balm nor Tom's Storage have re-added their JEI integration yet, hence the errors logged by JEI.

> Exception while loading entries for entrypoint 'jei_mod_plugin' provided by 'balm'
> Exception while loading entries for entrypoint 'jei_mod_plugin' provided by 'toms_storage'

That means no Balm code is actually running (or even present) in response to JEI being loaded.

If there is a memory leak after adding JEI, it is therefore more likely to be related to JEI itself.

[comment by The0GReborn (none)]
Thanks for clarifying! That makes sense—so the JEI exceptions are expected since Balm and Tom’s Storage haven’t re-added JEI integration for 1.21.11.

I understand now that any memory spikes I was seeing are likely caused by JEI itself and not by Balm. I’ll monitor JEI updates and adjust my setup accordingly.
